newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: Japan spot expiry fails to lift Singapore rubber.
newsitem.headline: Japan spot expiry fails to lift Singapore rubber.

text.p: The spot expiry in Japan did not give the Singapore rubber market much of a lift at the close of quiet dealings on Monday with only light shortcovering seen for RSS1 and TSR20 rubber, dealers said.
"There was some shortcovering for RSS1 and forward deliveries of TSR20, but the volume of action was a bit thin. The spot expiry in Japan did not have too much of an impact here," a dealer said.
"The offtake was not very heavy," another dealer said. "Nothing really moved through most of the day. I don't think the big boys were very active today."

Traders said they were monitoring any further news of intervention by the Thai government in the local rubber market and some covering by European buyers. Chinese inquiries for latex in Malaysia provided backdrop to the market.
At 0945 GMT, July RSS3 was indicated at 114.50 U.S. cents a kg from 113.00 cents.
July RSS1 was indicated at 163.50 Singapore cents (US$1.14) a kg from 161.50 cents.
July TSR20 was indicated at 155.75 Singapore cents (US$1.09) a kg from 154.75 cents.
